strings.en: The honeybees of Janthir are an incredibly pragmatic subspecies. When bonded to an individual, or the hive's queen as they most often are, the bees are incredibly chivalrous toward their proprietor. However, I'd be remiss if I didn't mention their stingers. Likely adapted to protect themselves from the treacherous nature of the region, the Janthiri bee's ovipositor is markedly durable and even more hazardous. The lowland kodan often coat their weapons in bee venom before a challenging hunt. —Acht

The root has dried and it may take a full dragon cycle to replenish... As such, the elders have convened and my word is final. We will leave Castora. If we wish to protect our legacy, it is the only way.    
  
Most of the elders have given themselves to the All Seer, while the rest prepare for battle. We look at the young with heavy eyes... They remind me so much of you. Daring and proud; clinging to their every conviction until torn from their corpse. 
  
Many of our people will scatter to the stretches of this plane, and I will give them the only gift I'm able to now: time. Tomorrow, we will voyage to the isles of Janthir, where I will lead what I hope to be a final assault against the mursaat. It may be a fool's hope, but if we can strike down Yagon, if we can diminish her ranks...perhaps that will be enough. Even if I face the most damning of fates, it will give our people time to hide.  
  
Would you grin, seeing me squirm? Or would you pity me? These are the days I might admit to missing your counsel.
Your guild has claimed Windswept Haven and is holding it against recapture by the Mordant Crescent.

*This letter is made to appear as though it is just a collection of observations about the local wildlife, but it actually contains a different missive hidden within.*

While my survey of the island is ongoing, I am confident already in the assessment that control over it would be economically and strategically worthwhile. There is an unexpected population present, but they occupy a very small portion of the available land; even if we were to cede them that portion entirely, it would have no meaningful impact on the viability of the project.  
  
It would, however, be a substantial undertaking due to the remaining defenses and the difficult landscape. It is unclear when sufficient transportation to make this possible will be achieved, but it seems likely to happen eventually. Overall, I would say the project is viable and the rewards exceedingly worthwhile. There is more potential here than anywhere else remaining in Tyria.  
  
However, if an attempt is to be made, I would strongly encourage the ministry to move quickly, because we are not the only ones who have taken an interest. I won't speculate on the viability of political maneuvering to lay claim to it; I am certain the Ministry of Law could find cause to claim ownership of the sun and stars if they so chose. But more aggressive approaches should be considered as well. Someone will wind up in control of Castora by the end of this, and we'd best make sure that it's us.  
  
—M
